kinds.text: A vote to end debate so the Senate can move to a final vote. On nominations it needs only a simple majority. Passing cloture isn't the final vote.
kinds.source: Senate Rule XXII; precedents of Nov. 21, 2013 and Apr. 6, 2017
kinds.when: The vote needed a simple majority (cloture on a nomination)

kinds.text: A vote to end debate so the Senate can move to a final vote. On a bill it needs three-fifths of senators sworn in, 60 when the Senate is full. Passing cloture doesn't pass the bill.
A vote to end debate on whether to take up a bill. It needs three-fifths of senators sworn in, 60 when the Senate is full. Passing it lets the Senate start on the bill, not pass it.
questions: On Cloture on the Motion to Proceed

kinds.text: Senate: whether to start debating a bill at all.
The confirmation vote. A simple majority.
kinds.source: U.S. Constitution, Art. II, Sec. 2; Senate Rule XXXI

kinds.text: The vote to approve a treaty. It needs two-thirds of senators present.
kinds.source: U.S. Constitution, Art. II, Sec. 2; Senate Rule XXX

kinds.text: House fast track for bills with broad support. Short debate, no amendments, needs two-thirds.

kinds.text: Ends debate on a rule and blocks changes to it. Usually splits by party. Not a vote on the bill.
kinds.when: The measure is a special rule: an H.Res. providing for the consideration of a bill

kinds.text: Ends debate on the resolution and blocks changes to it, bringing it straight to a vote. Not the vote on the resolution itself.
Sets the terms for debating a bill: time, amendments allowed. Not the bill itself.
kinds.when: The measure is a special rule: an H.Res. providing for the consideration of a bill
questions: On Agreeing to the Resolution, as Amended

kinds.text: Whether the House will take up the resolution at all.
The vote on the measure itself. Passing sends it to the other chamber, or to the President once both have passed it. A simple majority.
The vote on the joint resolution itself. Like a bill, once both chambers pass it, it goes to the President, unless it proposes a constitutional amendment.
A vote to adopt a resolution. A resolution doesn't go to the President and doesn't become law.
kinds.when: The measure is not a special rule
questions: On Agreeing to the Resolution, as Amended

kinds.text: A resolution both chambers adopt, such as a budget resolution. It doesn't go to the President and isn't law.
A vote to override a veto. It needs two-thirds of those voting, in each chamber.
kinds.source: U.S. Constitution, Art. I, Sec. 7, cl. 2
questions: Passage, Objections of the President To The Contrary Notwithstanding

kinds.text: The vote on the final text House and Senate negotiators agreed on. It can't be amended.
A vote to change the measure's text. Adopting an amendment doesn't pass the measure.
questions: On Agreeing to the Amendment, as Modified

kinds.text: A vote to change the measure's text. Adopting an amendment doesn't pass the measure.
Whether the House accepts the Senate's changes, so both chambers have passed the same text.
questions: On Motion to Concur in the Senate Amendment
On Motion to Concur in the Senate Amendments

kinds.text: The House accepts the Senate's changes with a further change of its own, which goes back to the Senate.
questions: On Motion to Concur in the Senate Amendment with an Amendment

kinds.text: Whether to negotiate a final version with the Senate in a conference committee.
questions: On Motion to go to Conference

kinds.text: Tells the House's negotiators what position to take with the Senate. The instruction isn't binding.
The minority's last motion before passage: send the bill back to committee. Rarely passes.
The minority's motion to send the measure to a committee instead of voting on it now. Rarely passes.
questions: On Motion to Commit with Instructions

kinds.text: Whether to send the measure back to committee.
Whether to send the measure to a committee instead of acting on it now.
Whether to send the measure to a committee instead of acting on it now.
Sets the item aside, which in practice kills it.
questions: On Motion to Table the Motion to Discharge Committee

kinds.text: Sets the item aside, which in practice kills it.
Sets aside a motion to reconsider, which makes the vote just taken final.
Whether to vote again on a question already decided.
Whether to vote again on a question already decided.
Takes a measure away from a committee that hasn't acted on it, so the House can vote on it. It comes up once a majority of the House has signed a discharge petition.

Whether to take a measure away from the committee holding it so the full Senate can act on it. These votes come under laws that fast-track certain measures, such as war powers and arms sales resolutions.
kinds.source: Expedited-procedure statutes, e.g. the War Powers Resolution (50 U.S.C. 1546a)

kinds.text: Whether to end the day's sitting now.
Whether to end the day's sitting now.
A quorum call: members record that they are present. Nothing is decided.
kinds.source: House Rule XX, clauses 5-7; U.S. Constitution, Art. I, Sec. 5

kinds.text: Directs the Sergeant at Arms to ask absent senators to come to the chamber, so there is a quorum.
Whether the Senate upholds an objection that the pending business breaks its rules or a law that binds it, such as the Budget Act.
Whether the presiding officer's ruling on the rules stands.
questions: On the Decision of the Chair

kinds.text: The House elects its Speaker by calling each member's name. Winning takes a majority of those who vote for a person by name.
kinds.source: U.S. Constitution, Art. I, Sec. 2, cl. 5
